interface_detail: a Worker binding; RPC and WebSocket to the object
tooling: Wrangler, the Workers runtime, SQLite storage per object
chaining: a stateful coordination point with a WebSocket, which is a relay substrate and not a general machine

limits.value: 13,000 GB-s of duration a day; a WebSocket held open on the non-hibernation API bills for the whole connection
128 MB of memory per object, billed as a full 128 MB regardless of use

limits_note: a Durable Object stays active while a request, response stream, WebSocket or pending I/O is in flight
notes: It is a Durable Object allowance and attributing it to Workers was a category error.

free_tier.stated: 13,000 GB-seconds of Durable Object duration a day on the free plan. That is a Durable Object allowance; Workers Free separately carries 100,000 requests a day
free_tier.notes: an object that is idle and eligible for hibernation is not billed for duration; duration is billed for the 128 MB allocation regardless of actual use

retention.stated: SQLite-backed storage persists; hibernation disconnects clients without destroying state

egress.terms: served from the edge; no per-byte charge on the limits page

identity_cost.detail: a Cloudflare account; no card for the Free plan

evidence.proved: the included allocation table reads 'Duration | 13,000 GB-s / day | 400,000 GB-s / month, + $12.50/million GB-s'
'Durable Objects that are idle and eligible for hibernation are not billed for duration'; duration is billed for the 128 MB allocation regardless of actual usage
Workers Free carries 100,000 requests a day; the page does not carry the 13,000 GB-s figure

session_cap.note: no idle kill while connected; duration billed only while active

keep_rate.basis: duration is billed only while active

network_out.ports: HTTP and WebSocket through the edge

binding_note: the daily duration allocation binds before the 128 MB ceiling, and a non-hibernating WebSocket spends it at wall-clock rate
